html:
A North Germanic people of southern Sweden, in the region still called Götaland, the land of the Geats. The map shows them in 400.

Ptolemy seems to mention them in the 2nd century, and 6th century writers such as Jordanes and Procopius name them among the peoples of Scandinavia. They are best known from the Old English poem Beowulf, whose hero is a Geat. The poem tells of the Geatish king Hygelac, who died raiding the lower Rhine. The Frankish historian Gregory of Tours records a real northern king, Chlochilaichus, killed on such a raid around 516, so the poem keeps a memory of real events.

Over the Middle Ages the Geats and the Swedes to their north joined into one kingdom, the root of Sweden; the map shows that stage as Swedes and Goths. Whether the Geats are connected to the Goths has been argued for centuries. Their name lives on in Götaland and in Gothenburg.
sum: A North Germanic people of southern Sweden, in the region still called Götaland, the land of the Geats. The map shows them in 400.
